row.premortem: If this fails, the most likely reason is that ancilla 4's mid-circuit readouts and resets disturb the data qubits enough, growing with each later measurement, that CNT2 reaches 0 in at least one of the four systems.
row.prior_work: **On every platform tried, Peres–Mermin exceeds its noncontextual bound of 4 in χ.** Two trapped ions with each observable read out sequentially: 5.46(4) (Kirchmair et al. 2009, Nature 460:494, arXiv:0904.1655). Google Willow (superconducting) with mid-circuit measurement and reset: 5.618 ± 0.005 (Kumar et al. 2025, arXiv:2512.02284; no CbD, marginal or signalling analysis). IBM Heron r2 ibm_kingston, product-only readout: 5.31, no error bars (Kelleher & Holweck 2025, arXiv:2505.21243). 2019-era 5-qubit IBM devices: about 4.99 (Laghaout et al. 2022, Eur. J. Phys. 43:055401, arXiv:2009.10751). **CbD:** the only CbD treatment of PM hardware data, Massé 2021 (arXiv:2105.13821, unrefereed; an adapted, not exact, formula), leaves Kirchmair's data contextual by 0.566; the exact CbD 2.0 LP gives CNT2 ≥ 0.141 on the same published numbers under every completion (`map/reads/p3-9-desk-work-2026-11-05.md`, `8b95dbd`). **Prior work predicts a pass for both input states.** No exact CbD LP has been applied to PM data from superconducting hardware, and no CbD analysis of sequential superconducting PM data was found (three searches, 2026-11-05, in the desk-work note, the third in another field's words: "state-independent contextuality … sequential QND … signalling disturbance correction"). **What this bet adds:** the exact CbD 2.0 LP with a CNT2 bootstrap on sequential mid-circuit-measurement data from an IBM Heron r2 (ibm_fez), in both measurement orders and for two input states; program 1's check pointed where physics fixes the answer. It is an instrument check, not a new physics claim. The engine's odds (80) sit near what the prior work predicts; the 20 points left for a fail price the device's mid-circuit measurement and reset errors, which no published IBM PM test exposed to CbD.
